messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are cracking, but only in places no one can see—yet. The generals are still marching in step, the markets are quiet, and the hospitals aren’t full of nervous breakdowns. But the rich are selling their gold, the bureaucrats are tripping over themselves, and the foreign kids keep showing up like nothing’s wrong. That’s the scariest part: they’re still one step ahead of us. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this isn’t the time to be the first to blink."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting quieter—not because they’re healing, but because no one dares to tap them. The regime’s grip feels tighter than ever, but even the elite are betting on the long game, not the exit. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for safety."*"
Sender 3: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but just barely—like a stack of plates someone’s trying not to drop. The guards aren’t pushing, the markets are still open, and the bosses are still signing papers… but everything’s slower, quieter, like we’re all waiting for the next gust of wind. Keep your ears open—small things might mean more than they seem."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting underfoot, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the wind. The usual channels are holding for now, but the cracks are showing in the weirdest ways—paychecks late, memes too bold, even the bots tripping over themselves. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. If something’s coming, it won’t be quiet."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels different—like they’re breathing easier, but the walls are still listening. The usual whispers are there, but they’re careful, like people testing the wind before stepping out. For now, the machine keeps humming, but don’t mistake quiet for stillness."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s cracking in places—no one’s rushing to fix it, just whispering about whether it’s worth repainting at all. The shopkeepers are betting on the house, but the bookies are sweating, and that’s what worries me."*"
Sender 7: "*"The air feels different—like something’s loosening, but no one’s sure if it’s a crack or just a little give in the rope. The usual players are moving again, but the guards are watching their own steps more than ours. Keep your eyes open, but don’t change your pace yet—this could be the calm before the storm, or just the wind shifting."*"
Sender 8: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath, but no one wants to be the first to exhale. The machine’s still running, but the gears are grinding slower, and the fuel’s getting expensive. Let’s keep our heads down, but stay sharp—this isn’t over, and the wrong move could make it worse."*"
Sender 9: "*"Things feel strangely calm—too calm. The usual cracks aren’t showing, but the quiet ones are starting to talk, and the regime’s letting them. If this is a show, it’s a good one… but even the best acts have a limit."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting louder—memes in the open, jokes in the streets, even the bank’s ‘corrections’ feel like a script. The old hands are playing chess, not checkers, but the board’s wobbling. Keep your eyes open, not your mouths."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels lighter—checkpoints thinning, shops hiring, even the foreigners aren’t twitching. But the hospitals are running dry, and the old folks just want their quiet back. They’re not scared, just tired. We’re not invisible, but we’re not a storm either—yet."*"
Sender 12: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, just fresh paint. The usual whispers are still there, but the air feels heavier now, like everyone’s holding their breath for the same reason. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open."*"
Sender 13: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no panic, just the usual quiet hum. The big players are still all in their seats, and the streets? Too tired to even whisper. But the foreigners are packing up their non-essentials… so maybe we’re the only ones who don’t see the storm yet."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are in the foundation—not the paint. The kids are still going to school, the trash is piling up, and the banks are whispering about ‘temporary’ rules. Nobody’s panicking, but nobody’s *hopeful* either. Let’s keep our eyes open and our mouths quiet—this isn’t the time to test the air, but it might be the time to prepare for when the wind changes."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, no panic, just the usual quiet grumbling. But the air feels heavier than it should, like everyone’s holding their breath without realizing it. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels different—less like the old quiet, more like the calm before something shifts. The regime’s showing its teeth, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, but don’t let fear make the decisions for you."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting underfoot, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the first tremors. The top’s still holding, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could go either way."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath, but no one’s ready to move yet. The usual cracks are showing, but the walls are still standing… for now. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. We’ll know soon enough if the ground shifts."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are cracking—small things, but the kind that don’t get fixed unless someone’s really paying attention. Keep your heads down, but if you’ve got a quiet way to test the wind, now might be the time to listen for how it blows back."*"
Sender 20: "*"The jokes are getting louder, but the paychecks are still coming—and the elites aren’t running. The regime’s got cracks, but they’re the kind that let in light, not the kind that bring the roof down. Still, watch the fuel lines—if the price stays high, we’ll know who’s really in control."*"
Sender 21: "*"Things are holding, but it’s like walking a tightrope—one wrong step and the whole thing could wobble. The machine’s still running, but everyone’s bracing for the next jolt, and the ones who know best are quietly making sure they’ve got an exit if the wind changes."*"
Sender 22: "*"The machine is still running, but the gears are grinding louder than usual—too many small things slipping through the cracks, too many old voices suddenly whispering the same warnings. The regime’s showing its teeth, but I don’t think it’s as hungry as it wants us to believe. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake exhaustion for surrender."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are thinner than they seem—people are talking, even the ones who should know better. The ship’s still afloat, but the crew’s arguing over who’s at the wheel, and the lifeboats are being checked. Let’s keep our eyes open, but our heads down—this could be the calm before the storm, or just another false dawn."*"
Sender 24: "*"The ship’s still afloat for now—payments are steady, the streets are quiet, and even the usual malcontents seem to have lost their fire. But don’t mistake calm for stability; the clinic’s stocking up, the airlines are adding flights, and the right people are whispering about who’s *not* at the wheel. Keep your eyes open, but don’t move yet—this isn’t the time to test the water."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are thicker than they look—no cracks, just a quiet hum of things settling. The old hands have stopped whispering, and the new ones don’t even ask questions anymore. Let’s keep our eyes open, but maybe we’ve been holding our breath for nothing."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
